title: A dungeon crawl for ants? The Abandons (review)
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kb2G7jcB3Ls

A whiplash review: straight from the table-swallowing Fallen Land, Daniel (@dungeondive) pulls out The Abandons, possibly the smallest and simplest game he owns, found used after two years of watching eBay. It is a solo-only card-laying labyrinth of about 50 cards that plays in five to fifteen minutes, a proper coffee-break game to sit beside Quests Over Coffee. Place the exit at the bottom of the deck, start on the stairwell, and follow each door's diamond count to draw one or two cards. Junctions offer choices, dead ends send you back to the last junction with an unexplored path, and if there is none the game is over, doors closing behind you as you go. Item cards combine into a map that lets you peek at and reorder the top three cards at a crossroads, a bomb that blasts through a wall, and a magic mirror that returns you to the entrance. Stairs let you descend and effectively start fresh. Daniel plays three games on camera and loses all three, one within a few draws, and puzzles over a walled card the rules never mention. His verdict is candid: it is a trifle, dungeon solitaire, that grew on him the more he played, fits in a palm, and might be worth an impulse buy, though probably not a hunt.

----

Daniel calls The Abandons "dungeon solitaire". Is there a game you keep purely as a five-minute ritual, and what makes it worth the shelf space?
